ask:
Brief, copied from briefs/c22-windows-installer-and-rm-shim.md and kept in step with it. Paste all of it to a claude-settings session. Sent Oct 21 as lanes W1 to W3 of the running batch.

Added work for your current batch: Windows process churn. Roadmap step c22 (stop the Mac/Linux installer and rm shim running on Windows). Finish or park the lane you are in first; do not restart lanes already done. These lanes are small and urgent, so land them as soon as your current lane allows, in this same batch. If they cannot share a batch, open them as their own small batch that merges first. They fix existing code on a platform it was never meant for. No measuring; prove each fix with a test.

Why: on the owner's Windows machine (Git Bash, no admin), RAM climbs to about 98% over a day and only a reboot clears it. Kernel memory grows with every process start. The worst offender caught was the rm shim: 4 processes (sh, a forked sh, the WindowsApps python3 alias, the real python) on every rm -rf.

Checked at 5584d1b:
- The settings.json SessionStart hook (startup|resume) runs `bash "$d/install.sh"` whenever bash exists, so the Mac/Linux installer runs on Windows at every session start.
- landed-dirs.txt includes bin, so it lands bin/rm, whose header says "Posix only; install.ps1 does not land this file."
- install.sh (near line 600) adds ~/.claude/bin to PATH in ~/.bashrc, putting the shim first in Claude Code's shells. install.sh has no Windows check.
- bin/rm calls bare python3 (the WindowsApps alias on Windows, which starts a second python) and builds its Python with $(cat <<'PYEOF'), one more fork.

Lane W1, the installer stays off Windows. The SessionStart hook skips install.sh when uname -s is MINGW*, MSYS* or CYGWIN*, and install.sh exits 0 at its top on those, naming install.ps1 as the Windows installer. Test both. Record the ruling in place under decisions/ (one ruling, a one-line reason).

Lane W2, the rm shim. On MINGW, MSYS or CYGWIN, exec the real rm at once, before any python. Elsewhere, find Python the way the hooks do (python3 then python, skip WindowsApps), and pass the Python on stdin with a here-doc instead of $(cat). Mac and Linux protection stays exactly as it is. Test the Windows exec path, the WindowsApps skip, and the existing refusal cases.

Lane W3, ci_wake's pre-filter. Tighten the PostToolUse shell pre-filter from any "ready" to the phrase gh pr ready, so other commands start no python. The watch itself, its deadline and asyncRewake stay.

Overlap with your current lanes: W1 and W3 edit settings.json, which your 'if' filter lane also edits. Do them in one pass on settings.json, or rebase whichever lands second; keep both sets of changes.

In your report, add:
- Per W lane: what changed and the test that proves it.
- A checklist the owner runs on the Windows machine after this merges and is pulled, no admin needed and nothing scripted: delete ~/.claude/bin/rm; remove the "# claude-settings: ~/.claude/bin on PATH" block from ~/.bashrc; check ~/.claude/claude-settings-install.log for install.sh runs; and check whether install.sh replaced ~/.claude/settings.json or a landed folder with something install.ps1 would not have made, and how to put it back.
note: Merged Oct 21, 17:22 CDT, in #552 (main 6c187c78) with c18 and c19: W1 #558, W2 #554, the parent-delete guard rule #557 and the hook lanes. Still open as drafts at 01:15 CDT Oct 22: #556 (manual memory monitor; your re-run after this batch needs it merged or run from its branch), #551 (settings if filters; looks superseded by your config_watch-only ruling, unchecked) and #549 (carried by #559). A follow-up lane, stale-postmerge-hook (install.ps1 removes its own post-merge hook when symlinks work, decision post-merge-hook-is-a-fallback), was built 00:34 to 00:58 and has no PR yet. Earlier state, 19:25 Oct 21: main is at 73ed71a; 13 draft PRs are open (W1 #558, W2 #554, the parent-delete guard rule #557, the memory monitor #556, and the c18/c19 batch #552 with its parts #546 to #553, #555); none is ready, and CI skips every job on a draft (decision draft-until-reviewed), so none has a CI verdict yet. Main still runs install.sh at every Windows session start (settings.json line 160). Verified at 5584d1b. The SessionStart hook runs install.sh whenever bash exists, so the Mac/Linux installer runs on Windows at every session start and resume. It lands bin/ (the rm shim included, though its header says Posix only) and puts ~/.claude/bin first on PATH through ~/.bashrc. The shim calls bare python3, which on Windows is the WindowsApps alias (2 pythons), plus an extra fork for $(cat). ci_wake starts python for any command containing 'ready', though only gh pr ready starts a watch. Seen on your machine Oct 21: install.sh ran three times back to back from 11:51, each 80 to 90 s, against the hook's 20 s timeout, so each run is orphaned and every session start launches another. Running now: lanes W1 to W3, added to the hook import and process-start batch (c18, c19). After it merges: your cleanup checklist from the brief, then re-run the memory monitor. ci_wake, checked at 5584d1b: a real watch keeps one python alive up to 55 min (deadline 3300 s) and starts gh every 30 s, about 110 gh starts per watch. Your pick, Oct 21 (sent as a follow-up to the running session): keep the narrowed trigger and the deadline, back the status reads off from 30 s to about 120 s (roughly 4x fewer gh starts, up to 2 min later wake). The follow-up also asks the session to run the cleanup itself after W1 and W2 are pulled, and to record the if-filter probe in the hook-if-filters decision. W2 question, Oct 21: the shim refuses rm -rf of home, a parent folder and '.', and guard.py lacks '.', '..' and parent-of-cwd. Advice sent: W2 as briefed, and move those refusals into guard.py's existing recursive-delete rule (Bash and PowerShell, with tests); not a new rule, and no freeze is in force. Refined answer sent: tests cover spelling variants (./, -r -f, -fr, --recursive, quoted, absolute cwd in /c/ and C:\ forms, PowerShell Remove-Item -Recurse and its aliases), cd .. && rm -rf . is refused, and rm -rf ./build and a sibling folder stay allowed. Accepted risk, Windows only: a delete inside a script, a runtime variable or a symlink to a parent is not caught (the shim still catches those on Mac and Linux), recorded in the W1 decision record. W1 CI, Oct 21: two Windows tests faked a Linux uname to keep passing (the gates-windows install.sh suite, which timed out on #544's run, and the install.sh leg of install-set.test.ps1). Your answer: drop both and close debt install-checkout-flake; one fast Windows test under the real Git Bash uname proves install.sh exits 0, writes nothing to ~/.claude and prints one skip line; check every Windows caller first. Checked at 5584d1b: merge/install_from_main.sh already runs install.ps1 on Windows, the Windows post-merge hook (written by install.ps1) runs install.ps1, and only the SessionStart hook ran install.sh. After W1, Windows refreshes on pull and merge, not at session start. Correction, Oct 21: the dropped install-suite step also ran caseF1 and caseG1, which test session_start.sh (real Windows code); your answer: keep them on Windows in their own short-timeout CI step and reopen debt install-checkout-flake, retired only by fixing the race; the debt records which side the race is on, and if it is in session_start.sh itself it is a live Windows bug at session start and gets raised. Advisor pick, Oct 21: start no new batch until this one lands; land it first. Found Oct 21 by the running session: ~/.claude/bin/rm has CRLF on your machine, so its line-2 marker check misses, it execs itself in a loop, and every rm in a Claude Bash shell hangs. install.sh copies it from the checkout at each session start, so a plain delete does not stick. Advice sent: a stopgap that survives session starts, with no push: bin/* text eol=lf in the checkout's .git/info/attributes, rewrite bin/rm through /usr/bin/rm and git checkout, fix the ~/.claude copy, stop only its own loops, and report core.autocrlf and git ls-files --eol for other CRLF files. Then keep the plan: the tracked eol=lf rule in the fix PR (bin/* and any other CRLF file found), and delete the shim and its PATH line after W1 and W2 merge. Pin line endings, Oct 21: main's .gitattributes has no bin/* eol=lf rule (only *.cmd crlf and one run.sh line); W2 (#554) carries it. Under autocrlf=true, four bin files in the current pin are CRLF (merge, verdict, ste-changed, claude-janitor), The session measured that verdict and merge run fine with CRLF, since Python and Node ignore a CR (the advisor's guess that they were broken was wrong). Of 108 tracked #! files, 105 are Python or Node; 3 are shell scripts, where a CR does break the run: githooks/main-ref/reference-transaction, skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable and bin/claude-janitor. Advice sent: scope the rule and test to shell scripts only, so 100+ .py files don't churn in every Windows checkout. The rule is bin/* githooks/* *.sh text eol=lf, plus the impeccable script by path. W1's CI test checks each landed ~/.claude/bin entry links to or is byte-equal to the pin. It also fails on a CR in *.sh or in any #! file whose interpreter is sh, bash or zsh (directly or through env), red on main and green on the batch. No new install code. Home for the rule, advice sent Oct 21: a new decision, shell-scripts-check-out-lf, not rm-path-wrapper (the shim's record), since the rule covers every shell script; rm-path-wrapper points to it. Checked at 73ed71a: no decision covered line endings. #552's second run, Oct 21: red on the Ruling kind check (shell-scripts-check-out-lf had Kind: build but no Plan: line); fixed in lane #554 under your new in-lane fix ruling (c30), not dropped. Next, Oct 21: one goal file, briefs/cleanup-goal-oct21.md, runs every remaining cleanup step in order after this batch (about 20 hours, one claude-settings session). Open, for IT: why processes under Claude start with about 2,000 handles against about 180 by hand. Goal session report, Oct 22: needs you: delete ~/.claude/bin/rm with the PowerShell line from earlier.
title: Stop the Mac/Linux installer and rm shim running on Windows
why: Your Windows audit, Oct 21: RAM climbs to about 98% over a day and only a reboot clears it, with kernel pool growing about 0.8 GB an hour while tool calls run. The longest-lived processes were the rm shim's 4-process chain. Process churn is the lever on our side; the rest (why each MSYS2 process starts with about 2,000 handles) goes to IT's security agents.
